errors: ops[7]: assertion has record_basis "absent" but record_role 'head_of_household' — these are two different fields that share the value: record_basis "absent" means the RECORD lacked the value, record_role "absent" means the PERSON was not in it — and negative evidence always uses the literal record_role "absent", and that holds even when the record NAMES the person: an obituary's "preceded in death by his wife, Ruth" is still negative evidence about her vital status, so her role is "absent", not "spouse_1". Before changing the role, check the finding is an ABSENCE at all. A fact about a person PRESENT in the record is record_basis "stated" carrying that person's real record_role — change both fields together, not just this one. A blank field on a present person (no surname, no occupation) is silence: write no assertion. If it is an absence, keep the person's identity in `value` (e.g. "Walter Whitaker preceded Harold Dean Whitaker in death"), not a generic value shared across multiple people. A conforming negative is exactly: record_role "absent", informant_proximity "researcher", informant "the researcher" — the attached worked example shows a record_basis "stated" assertion and does not satisfy this rule.

What has changed is the honest account of who provided it and how reliable that person's knowledge of the birth event could be. Logged as log_001. Now delegating: **1 of 1** — Pennsylvania Certificate of Death for Patrick Flynn, March 12, 1908, Shenandoah, Schuylkill County.

---

This 1908 Pennsylvania death certificate names Patrick Flynn, a 63-year-old coal miner, who died on March 12, 1908, in Shenandoah, Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania, of miners' asthma (pneumoconiosis) after a three-year illness. His wife Mary Flynn, living at 214 Main St in Shenandoah, gave the information for the certificate; she reported that Patrick was born in Ireland, that his father was Thomas Flynn (also born in Ireland), and that his mother's maiden name was Mary Brennan (also born in Ireland). The attending physician Dr. William H. Stein certified the cause of death, and undertaker J.J. Franey arranged burial on March 15, 1908, at Annunciation Cemetery in Shenandoah.

The next step is for the person-evidence skill to evaluate whether this record's deceased persona is Patrick Flynn (I1) in the family tree, and if so to create the identity link so the certificate's facts appear on his tree profile.

errors: ops[15]: assertion has record_basis "absent" but informant_proximity 'self' — negative evidence is the researcher's own conclusion, so it always takes informant_proximity "researcher": no record informant reported an absence, whatever the record type, and that holds even when the record names the person (the "preceded in death by" shape). Set informant_proximity to "researcher". Only if the finding is not an absence at all — a fact about a person present in the record — is "absent" the wrong record_basis, and then record_role must change from "absent" to that person's real role in the same edit; changing record_basis alone is refused. A conforming negative is exactly: record_role "absent", informant_proximity "researcher", informant "the researcher" — the attached worked example shows a record_basis "stated" assertion and does not satisfy this rule.

errors: ops[14]: assertion has record_basis "absent" but record_role 'father_of_deceased' — these are two different fields that share the value: record_basis "absent" means the RECORD lacked the value, record_role "absent" means the PERSON was not in it — and negative evidence always uses the literal record_role "absent", and that holds even when the record NAMES the person: an obituary's "preceded in death by his wife, Ruth" is still negative evidence about her vital status, so her role is "absent", not "spouse_1". Before changing the role, check the finding is an ABSENCE at all. A fact about a person PRESENT in the record is record_basis "stated" carrying that person's real record_role — change both fields together, not just this one. A blank field on a present person (no surname, no occupation) is silence: write no assertion. The 1850 United States Census for Branch Township, Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania records a household headed by Thomas Flynn, with a boy named Patrick Flynn listed in the same household.
